description:
Returns a company's supply chain as the SEC annual reports state it: the suppliers it names and the customers that name it, each graded sole source, primary supplier or named, with the year the link was first reported, the share of revenue or of the input where a filing discloses one, and the sentence from the report with a link to it on SEC EDGAR. Also returns how many large companies name it as a supplier, how much of their market value depends on it, and links the reports stopped naming.

Use when the user asks who supplies a company, who its customers are, which companies depend on it, how concentrated its suppliers or customers are, or what is exposed if it stops supplying. Do not use it for valuation (use get_stock_valuation) or to search across companies (use screen_stocks).

Covers about 1,250 US-listed companies, from annual reports (10-K, 20-F) since 2013, updated nightly. Companies do not have to name their suppliers, so a missing link is not proof there is none. In Zyberno's tests these links did not predict share prices well enough to trade on: they describe a company and its risks.

symbol.description: Ticker symbol of a US-listed company, for example NVDA or TSM. Case insensitive.

name: get_supply_chain
